correctness.rationale: Passive Gaussian dynamics yields an exact two-mode matrix exponential and the analytic energy (1). For nonzero detuning the complex mode splitting has positive imaginary part bounded strictly below gamma/4 by dissipative stability. Differentiation gives a cosine versus positive convex hyperbolic envelope, leading to a rigorously finite turning-time cutoff. Strict concavity of the arccos envelope reduces derivative roots to two phase branches and gives N=omega*T/(2*pi)+O(1), with the stated singular coefficient. The resonant formula gives infinitely many maxima. Standalone code independently matched 300 matrix-exponential energies and 80 post-cutoff inequalities plus count tests. Numerics are corroboration, not infinite or uniqueness proof.

originality.rationale: The originating March 2024 article gives an equal-frequency pulsed oscillator formula and does not count detuned charging cycles. Actual scientific-index, alias and source searches found no implication covering the singular off-resonant finite-versus-infinite maximum classification or the explicit 1/|detuning| coefficient. Earlier matrix exponentials and generic damped-mode theory remain acknowledged prior material. High-relevance source sections were examined, and inaccessible broader material is identified as residual uncertainty rather than declared noncovering.

value.rationale: Frequency mismatch is an intrinsic experimental calibration variable in coupled quantum battery hardware. The exact count of mathematically distinct recharge episodes and its 1/|detuning| divergence reveal a singular coherence-time boundary absent from source peak-height and charging-time optimizations. The explicit finite turning-time envelope gives a hard stopping bound. These are motivated global structural statements rather than a relabeled single evaluation; they do not assert experimentally resolvable cycles or quantum advantage.
